page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing 12 vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance provides 96.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high 1:8 memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Cache provisioning includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES cryptography acceleration, BMI2, and FMA.

The hardware configuration includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, requiring dependence on network-attached block storage for persistence. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Benchmark testing illustrates a noticeable divergence between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core tests show constrained execution speed, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 950.0 and a single-core stress-ng result of 1109.09, both landing in the bottom 25th percentile. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression performs in the bottom 10th percentile at 19.12 GB/sec.

When workloads leverage all 12 vCPUs, execution scales into average industry percentiles. Multi-core stress-ng scores reach 8830.76, while multi-core Geekbench achieves 4817.0, PassMark CPU registers 10083.99, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yields 42.44 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth clocks at 56.97 GB/sec, while write operations reach 48.69 GB/sec. In application benchmarks, the instance executes Redis SET operations at 9.13 million operations per second and handles PassMark database operations at 3240.47, whereas static web serving throughput measures lower at 6.29 GB/sec. Large language model inference on a medium 7B model remains slow due to the lack of dedicated acceleration, generating 7.32 tokens per second.

Qualitatively, the ecs.r5.3xlarge provides resource density that favors RAM footprint over high per-thread computational velocity. The primary operational tradeoff involves accepting modest single-core execution speed and the absence of integrated local storage in exchange for significant memory capacity and stable multi-threaded execution. This balance makes the instance appropriate for in-memory caching systems, distributed data stores, mid-tier enterprise databases, memory-centric ETL pipelines, and data processing tasks where working sets require up to 96 GB of RAM.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 12 vCPUs across 6 physical cores of an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz, paired with 96.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local storage, contains no GPUs, and operates on a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data shows modest single-core throughput, including a Geekbench single-core score of 950.0, contrasted with solid multi-threaded performance, as indicated by a PassMark CPU score of 10083.99 and a multi-core Geekbench result of 4817.0. Memory throughput reaches 56.97 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads, and Redis SET throughput measures 9.13 million operations per second. With an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, the ecs.r5.3xlarge delivers cost-effective memory density for mid-sized in-memory databases, Redis caches, data transformation jobs, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
